name: marketing-hero
summary: The top of a landing page: an optional small eyebrow, a huge uppercase headline with one word in lime, one supporting line, a lime primary and a glass secondary call to action, and a showcase of one to three images.
useWhen: A landing or product page opens with one bold promise and a way to start, followed by examples of the work.
The page introduces one tool or feature and needs a headline, two actions and a visual of results.

alternatives.name: feature-grid
alternatives.when: the section lists several features rather than opening the page

alternatives.name: empty-state
alternatives.when: the screen is inside the app and nothing has been made yet

rules.do: Set one word or short phrase of the headline in lime, the word that carries the promise.
rules.dont: Set the whole headline in lime, or two separate words; the accent stops pointing anywhere.

rules.do: Fill the showcase with examples of what the product makes, each with alt text that says what it shows.
rules.dont: Use abstract gradients or screenshots of settings; a hero sells the result.

rules.do: Keep the headline under about eight words so it holds two or three lines at full size.
rules.dont: Put a paragraph in the headline; long uppercase text is hard to read.

a11y: The headline is the page's `h1`; use one hero per page.
Calls to action are links when given an `href` (rendered as buttons visually) and buttons otherwise.
Every showcase image needs `alt` text describing what it shows. The side images hide on narrow screens.
